([[Canberra]], [[Australian Capital Territory|ACT]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2022–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 49 | draft_team = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[BA Centre of Excellence]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team2 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team3 = →[[Cleveland Charge]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] ([[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman team (2023) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|AUS}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Asia Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2022 FIBA Asia Cup|2022 Jakarta]]|}} }} '''Tyrese Darnell Proctor''' (born 1 April 2004) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] and was drafted with the 49th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the Cleveland Cavaliers. ==Early life and career== Proctor was born in [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]],{{cite web |title=Tyrese Proctor - 2024-25 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyrese-proctor/20755 |website=Duke University |access-date=27 June 2025 |language=en}} to an Australian mother and an American-born father. His father, Rod, is a former professional basketball player for the [[Sydney Kings]] in Australia's [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]].{{cite web |last=Haigh |first=Paul |title=Tyrese Proctor helps NSW to silver at Pacific School Games |url=https://www.theleader.com.au/story/3572716/tyrese-proctor-helps-nsw-to-silver-at-pacific-school-games/ |website=St George and Sutherland Shire Leader |access-date=11 May 2022 |date=3 January 2016}} Proctor attended [[Bangor Public School (New South Wales)|Bangor Public School]] throughout his upbringing{{cite web |title=Trinitarian's pathway to basketball elite |url=https://www.trinity.nsw.edu.au/2022/05/05/tyrese-proctor-wins-duke-scholarship/ |website=Trinity Grammar School |date=5 May 2022}} and grew up playing an array of sports such as [[cricket]], [[soccer]] and [[baseball]] but basketball was his highest priority.{{cite web |last=Sweet |first=Nicole |title=Pro Insight - Tyrese Proctor |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/tyrese-proctor |website=Prospective Insight |access-date=5 April 2022 |date=18 January 2022}} He began playing junior basketball for the Sutherland Sharks and represented his home state of New South Wales at numerous national championships.{{cite web |last=G |first=Ayush |title=College, NBL or G League: What's next for Tyrese Proctor? |url=https://pickandroll.com.au/p/college-nbl-or-g-league-whats-next |website=Pick and Roll Australia |access-date=28 March 2022 |date=26 March 2022}} In 2021, Proctor received a scholarship to attend the [[NBA Global Academy]] in [[Canberra]].{{cite web |last=Dinjaski |first=Melanie |title=How rising Boomers star took 'huge step' at NBA Global Academy in Canberra before Duke basketball journey |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7881852/from-canberra-to-the-deep-south-boomers-star-on-path-to-the-nba/ |website=Canberra Times |access-date=10 November 2022 |date=8 November 2022}} He played for the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in the [[Waratah League]] in 2021, averaging 10.3 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists in seven games.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Proctor, Basketball Player, News, Stats - USbasket |url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Tyrese-Proctor/580009 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=27 June 2025 |url-access=subscription}} The following year, he played for the Centre of Excellence in the [[NBL1]] during the [[2022 NBL1 season|2022 season]], averaging 15.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 steals per game. While in Canberra, Proctor attended [[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra College]].{{cite web|url=https://www.lakeonline.act.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/543417/Issue_2_-_LAKENEWS_-_May.pdf|title=Lake News May 2022|work=[[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra College]]|access-date=27 June 2025|page=4}} ==College career== In April 2022, Proctor committed to join the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]].{{cite web |title=Teen Aussie 'top 20 prospect' signs for US college powerhouse |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/teen-aussie-top-20-prospect-signs-for-us-college-powerhouse/news-story/5b49fe9892686ec6356b5176ccc72c5c |website=Fox Sports Australia |access-date=10 November 2022 |date=8 April 2022}} He averaged 9.4 points and 3.3 assists per game as a freshman in the [[2022–23 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2022–23 season]], shooting 38.1% from the field. Proctor was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite news |last=Giles |first=Matt|title=Duke Basketball Sophomore Named Nation's No. 2 Breakout Star |url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/basketball/duke-basketball-sophomore-named-breakout-star-10-23 |access-date=21 February 2024 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=9 October 2023}} As a sophomore in [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2023–24]], Proctor played 32 games and averaged 10.5 points, three rebounds, and 3.7 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Proctor College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/tyrese-proctor-1.html |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |access-date=27 June 2025 |language=en}} As a junior in [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2024–25]], Proctor played 38 games and averaged 12.4 points, three rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game. In April 2025, Proctor declared for the [[2025 NBA draft|NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Jackson |first=Andrew |date=30 April 2025 |title=College stars, teenage giant and NBL talents as six Australians declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/nba-2025-five-australians-declare-for-the-nba-draft-alex-condon-tyrese-proctor-rocco-zikarksy-alex-toohey-ben-henshall/news-story/175c8f192ed13808c8252ced37cb8a54 |access-date=27 June 2025 |work=Fox Sports |language=en}} ==Professional career== On 26 June 2025, Proctor was selected by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with the 49th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Select Two Players in the 2025 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-2025-draft-250626|website=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2025|access-date=July 13, 2025}} On 1 July 2025, he signed a four-year, $8.69 million deal with the Cavaliers. The first two years were fully guaranteed, with a partially guaranteed third year, and a team option on the fourth year.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign 2025 Draft Pick Tyrese Proctor|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cavaliers-sign-2025-draft-pick-tyrese-proctor|website=NBNA.com|date=July 1, 2025|access-date=July 13, 2025}}{{Cite web|last=Scotto|first=Michael|date=1 July 2025|title=Second-round pick Tyrese Proctor signs four-year deal with Cavs|url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/second-round-pick-tyrese-proctor-signs-four-year-deal-with-cavs/|access-date=1 July 2025|website=HoopsHype|language=en-US}} On 3 March 2026, he was assigned to the [[Cleveland Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He appeared in a game for the Charge that day{{cite news |title=Charge Roll to Win on STEM Day |url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-roll-to-win-on-stem-day |access-date=1 June 2026 |work=cleveland.gleague.nba.com |date=3 March 2026}} before recalled to the Cavaliers immediately after.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Proctor Player Profile, Cleveland Cavaliers - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tyrese-Proctor/Summary/161766 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=1 June 2026 |language=en}} On 12 April, in the Cavaliers' regular season-finale, Proctor recorded 22 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists in a 130–117 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |title=Tyrese Proctor 2025-26 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/proctty01/gamelog/2026/ |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=1 June 2026 |language=en}} ==National team career== In February 2021, Proctor made his debut with the senior [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australia national team]] at the age of 16, in a [[2022 FIBA Asia Cup qualification|2022 FIBA Asia Cup qualifier]] against [[New Zealand men's national basketball team|New Zealand]].{{cite web |title=Tyrese Proctor 2022 FIBA Asia Cup qualifiers profile |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/192-fiba-asia-cup-qualifiers/208126/players/271242-tyrese-proctor |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=2 February 2022 |date=20 February 2021}} In July 2022, he returned to play for Australia in their [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|2023 FIBA World Cup qualifying]] win against [[China men's national basketball team|China]].{{cite web |last=Pitman |first=Kane |date=11 July 2022 |title=Tyrese Proctor eyes more Boomers minutes ahead of Duke move |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/34225631 |access-date=17 May 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} Later that month, he was selected to represent Australia at the [[2022 FIBA Asia Cup]] in [[Indonesia]], where he played a starring role in Australia's run to win the gold medal.{{cite web |date=25 July 2022 |title=Gold Medal Boomers Win Asia Cup Crown |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/gold-medal-boomers-win-asia-cup-crown |access-date=26 September 2022 |website=nbl.com.au}} In June 2026, Proctor was named in the Boomers squad for the next window of the [[2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers]] in Perth in July.{{cite news |title='Aussie Bryce' headlines Boomers' Qualifiers squad |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/aussie-bryce-cotton-headlines-boomers-qualifiers-squad |access-date=1 June 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=1 June 2026 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Hometown heroes and Boomers' debutants selected for Perth |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4509984/hometown-heroes-and-boomers-debutants-selected-for-perth |access-date=1 June 2026 |work=www.australia.basketball |date=1 June 2026 |language=en}}
